units.translation: The fuller and the nurse had the same end.
of the nourishment of an infant
which the recent scholiast explains by ἀνατροφαῖς [nourishment, upbringing].
where it is said of the payment for upbringing, in which sense τροφεία [maintenance, cost of upbringing] is used.
neither in my upbringing nor yet having reached manhood,
and in Argos paying back fair nurture,
and upon her children she invoked wrathful curses as their nurture.
then, wretched one, I was brought to your shores by my upbringing.
for repaying the favor of nurture.
for they did not rear me, nor did they grow old in nurture.
On fr. 192, 4 see under the word παντοτρόφος.
and to mother earth, dearest nurse.
through blood drunk up by the earth, the nurse.
and I see this nurse of Orestes in tears.
and nurse of the newly sown wave.

about which passage we have spoken under the word προσαυρίζω. With the form of the word, about which Lobeck spoke in Pathologiae Prolegomena p. 18, compare δρομή [running] said for δρόμος [running], which Arcadius noted p. 110, 10 and is read in Byzantine writers indicated in the Thesaurus vol. 2 p. 1684. τροχή [running] is not known from elsewhere.
moisture blowing upon the dry running.
of tents carried on chariots, ἀμφὶ σκηναῖς τροχηλάτοισιν [around wheeled tents].
the wheel-worn crossroads of the split road.
Scholiast: ἄγγελον, ἀπὸ τοῦ τρέχειν [messenger, from running].
for I see this runner of Zeus.
I am rolled like a wheel
and his eyes whirl in a circle.
and always the burden of the present evil will wear you out.
(with imperfect ἐτύγχανον, aorist ἔτυχον, future τεύξομαι) 1. to obtain, attain, become a partaker
2. τυγχάνω used absolutely, to hit the truth, to speak or act rightly
4. with a participle, signifying a chance occurrence
with the participle omitted, which is to be supplied from the preceding
with the participle of the substantive verb omitted
where before τεύξει one verse has fallen out in which was read the genitive of a substantive (such as τιμῆς), to which ὅσην refers.
where λέγων is to be understood from the preceding words of the other person, οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ὅπως λέξαιμι τὰ ψευδή καλά.
I was not deemed worthy to obtain this.
having obtained this deserted, neighborless hill.
it being possible for you to obtain a very great marriage.
that I may not obtain slavery.
for if they should obtain what they intend.
obtaining frequent clapping beneath the city.
you indeed will obtain many mourners.
and as many as remained and obtained safety.
he is gone, having obtained the three-thrower.
he will obtain all of his wits.
